answer: \(\text{For even } n: a_n = 0; \text{ for odd } n: a_n = -\frac{4L}{n^2\pi^2}\)

lq.q: Find the half-range cosine series for \(f(x)=x(\pi-x)\) in \((0,\pi)\). Hence, evaluate \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n^4}\).
answer: Step Marks Cosine series: \(f(x)=\frac{a_0}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_n\cos nx\) (1) \(a_0=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi}x(\pi-x)dx=\frac{\pi^2}{3}\) (2) \(a_n=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi}x(\pi-x)\cos nx\,dx=-\frac{2}{n^2}\) for \(n\geq1\) (4) Thus, \(x(\pi-x)=\frac{\pi^2}{6}-2\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{\cos nx}{n^2}\) (2) Using Parseval's: \(\frac{1}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi}[x(\pi-x)]^2dx=\frac{a_0^2}{4}+\frac{1}{2}\sum a_n^2\) ⇒ \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n^4}=\frac{\pi^4}{90}\) (6)
